findings.title: Define one literal-str alias function and account for NumPy formatting differences
findings.detail:
Add lizyml/codegen/column_names.py with one authoritative column_alias(label, *, source_format) function. Do not reuse plain_value or the category-value codec: those preserve values, whereas this rule intentionally produces column-name strings. Admit exact Python types str, int, float, bool, bytes, complex and NoneType; exact NumPy types str_, int8/16/32/64, uint8/16/32/64, float16/32/64, longdouble, bool_, bytes_, complex64/128, clongdouble, datetime64 and timedelta64. Platform aliases such as intp, float128 and complex256 are admitted when they resolve to one of these same types. Refuse every other type, including tuple labels, MultiIndex columns, Decimal, date/datetime objects, void scalars and arbitrary subclasses. Do not expand tuples or MultiIndex names. Also refuse an empty alias, an alias containing NUL, or text that cannot be UTF-8 encoded; these cannot satisfy the selected file-header contract consistently. These are export_code restrictions, not fit restrictions.

For admitted names, the alias is literally str(label), without .item(), repr(), numeric normalization, bytes decoding or temporal conversion. Thus int 7 becomes '7'; float 7.0 becomes '7.0'; -0.0 remains '-0.0'; NaN becomes 'nan'; infinities become 'inf'/'-inf'; booleans become 'True'/'False'; None becomes 'None'; bytes and numpy.bytes_(b'c') become "b'c'"; NumPy integers have no NumPy wrapper; complex values retain str() parentheses/signs; datetime64 and timedelta64 retain their unit-dependent str() text. Name collisions are determined from these resulting strings, including NaN/NaT aliases. Category values, including timedelta64 values subject to H-0139, never pass through this function.

Literal NumPy str() is not portable across the three lanes. Record column_name_format in both project JSON files: {numpy_version, numpy_legacy, longdouble_format}, where numpy_legacy is the export-time np.get_printoptions()['legacy'] and longdouble_format is [dtype.itemsize, finfo.nmant, finfo.maxexp]. For typed NumPy names other than str_, column_alias must require the recorded NumPy version and longdouble format, then evaluate str(label) under the recorded legacy printing option. A mismatch raises column_name_environment_mismatch before returning an alias. Python names and canonical string headers do not require a matching NumPy environment. This preserves literal export-time str(label) and prevents a generated validator from accepting a different alias silently. Existing requirements may remain unpinned; the boundary check is mandatory.

Embed this function and its small ValueError-compatible exception class into train.py and predict.py from the authoritative source, rather than maintaining a handwritten formatting implementation. DC3 tests must compare normalized function ASTs and execute the same accepted/refused fixtures against the library and both rendered copies, including format-environment mismatches and changed ambient printing options.

Executed evidence: scalar probes ran on pandas/NumPy 3.0.1/2.4.2, 2.3.3/2.2.6 and 2.0.0/1.24.0. A deterministic 5,036-scalar corpus had 310 differing alias texts between NumPy 2.4.2 and each older lane: 177 float16 and 133 float32 cases. For example, the same float16 prints '-1.279e+03' versus '-1279.0'; a float32 prints '3.879635e+10' versus '38796350000.0'. Legacy='1.13' also changed scalar text within one NumPy version. An in-memory prototype demonstrated source-format capture and explicit cross-version refusal. Supplemental fits confirmed Python bytes, Python complex, clongdouble, Decimal, empty-string and nonfinite-float numeric labels can work today; the stated Decimal/empty-string export refusals therefore must be documented explicitly.

findings.title: Preflight the complete project namespace at both export entrances before any write
findings.detail:
Run one shared project-name preflight in Model.export_code after obtaining fitted state and before the existing category-value preflight at line 415. Run it independently at generate_code entry, before build_config at generator.py:95. The facade check must still execute when generate_code is mocked. The generator must validate raw names before constructing any alias-keyed dictionary, creating directories, opening files, saving model text or writing source. Build an immutable projection of name-bearing containers; never rename or mutate the fitted state, configured roles, caller frame or saved models.

The namespace consists of ordered feature_names plus configured string references for target, time_col, group_col, features.exclude, features.categorical, split.blocks.col, split.groups.col and inner_valid.group_col. Include configured names even when absent from the feature frame: an explicit categorical reference '7' must not begin selecting an originally integer-named 7 after aliasing. Repeated references to the same string column are references, not separate physical columns; this permits blocked-split columns that are also genuine string features. A non-string feature whose alias equals any of these string references is a collision. Check duplicate feature aliases by position, without Python label equality or a set/dict of original labels: 7, True, 7.0 and NaN have problematic equality semantics. Separately check alias uniqueness within every name-keyed mapping and require projected category/mode/declared/identity/stand-in references to belong to the projected feature schema. A loaded declared-category key '7' may reference the same projected feature as original integer 7; it is not another physical column.

The closed new name-refusal reasons are column_name_collision and unsupported_column_name. Both raise LizyMLError(SERIALIZATION_FAILED), surface='export_code'. Context has surface, reason, kind, alias and columns. Each columns entry has where (the field path), position (zero-based within its list, or null for a scalar role), type (qualified name), repr (safe representation) and alias (string or null). Collision kind is duplicate_alias and reports every member of the first collision group. Unsupported kinds are type, empty_alias, invalid_alias_text, string_conversion_failed and unknown_reference. Scan unsupported names first, then collisions, in feature order followed by the role order above and the named state containers; diagnostics must be deterministic. Unsupported objects must not be stringified as a fallback. Native hand-off metadata validation described in the separate finding uses invalid_native_feature_metadata, not a misleading name refusal. Existing category-value errors retain their existing reasons.

Executed evidence: actual tiny fits with feature integer 7 and a separate string '7' used as target, time column, group column or excluded column all currently export successfully. The prototype namespace check identifies all four collisions. The typed-frame prototype rejected [7, '7'] with column_name_collision and both offending names. The source confirms current checks only concern category values, while artifact_writer.py:88 creates the directory before JSON serialization can reject a NumPy column label. No repository files were edited.

findings.title: Project aliases must cover every writer without changing runtime or category-value identity
findings.detail:
Use the validated projection at generator.py:95-129 and pass projected inputs to both writers. Retain input and feature order. Change the discovered-name annotations at generator.py:24-25 and _codegen_inputs.py:101-103 from string-only annotations to the accepted raw-name type; annotations must not pretend that fit already supplies strings.

The closed writer inventory is: config_writer.py:99/121 target reference; :111-114 declared-category dictionary keys; :126-127 feature_names and categorical_features; :138 categorical_rule.explicit; :150 inner_valid.group_col; :166 split.time_col, split.group_col, split.blocks.col and split.groups.col. All become or remain aliases. Add column_name_roles to config.json, with keys data.target, data.time_col, data.group_col, features.exclude, features.categorical, split.blocks.col, split.groups.col and inner_valid.group_col; each value is a list of string names, empty for an absent optional role. This records the complete reserved namespace, including exclusions that config.json currently omits.

For the copied native pipeline state, project feature_names, categorical_cols, encoder.categories keys, encoder.modes keys, encoder.identity_columns and encoder.stand_in_columns. artifact_writer.py:31-55 then emits alias feature/categorical lists, alias categories keys with the corresponding mode inside each entry, and alias identity/stand-in lists. It currently drops stand_in_columns: add that list explicitly. Carry the fitted stand-in plan in config.json too, and copy it into generated retraining state as provenance; generated transformation continues to encode categorical columns numerically and must not use this field to introduce another category policy. The generated train state writer at templates.py:385-397 must write the policy/format markers and these alias-only name fields itself, including after retraining.

values.py:26/70 remains the serializer for target/category values; do not alter its accepted value sets or stringify categories, modes, declared values, target classes, split cutoffs, metric parameters or other configuration values. identity_template.py:55-75 retains its existing category-identity membership logic after the project-name schema has been validated. Its values/temporal logic is unchanged. _codegen_inputs.py:30-39 and :42-98 continue resolving string group-role references. input_categories at :101-116 must continue collecting original typed keys before runtime preparation; projection happens only on the export copy. derived_sample_weight is a rule, not a column name.

Executed evidence: the reproduced pandas 3 matrix showed categories serialized under key '7' while identity_columns retained integer 7; generated prediction failed with 'pipeline_state.json has a malformed identity_columns'. Both pandas 2 lanes reproduced this failure. The copy/rekey prototype repaired all 29 fitted pandas 3 cases and all 30 fitted cases in each older lane. Runtime Model.export -> Model.load predictions had maximum absolute difference 0 for all fitted cases. Loaded declared-category metadata for integer 7 already had string key '7'; this existing persistence metadata loss is confirmed and remains outside this project-only change.

findings.title: Preserve LightGBM's positional categorical hand-off separately from alias names
findings.detail:
Aliasing categorical_features and passing those strings directly to LightGBM is insufficient to preserve retraining behavior. LightGBM interprets a Python integer in categorical_feature as a feature position, whereas a string is resolved as a name. The generated encoder's categorical_features must contain alias names, but the native training hand-off must preserve the positional declaration the fitted estimator actually used.

Add a required categorical_feature_indices list to ExportParams at lizyml/estimators/provider.py:33, populated by the sole production constructor, LGBMProvider.build_export_params at lizyml/estimators/lgbm/provider.py:593. Read the Dataset-resolved categorical_column declaration from the fitted Booster.params; absence means no native categorical declaration and is recorded as an explicit empty list. Validate it as a list of Python integer positions. Preserve positions as recorded, including out-of-range values; do not replace an original integer name with its current position or clamp an ignored position. Reject malformed native metadata before writes with SERIALIZATION_FAILED, surface='export_code', reason='invalid_native_feature_metadata', and where/type/repr context. This field is export metadata only; do not add fields to fitted/saved model state or alter fit.

Pass the list through _model_persistence.py:520, a required direct-generator argument, and config_writer.py as lgbm_categorical_feature_indices. Update direct-generator fixtures/callers explicitly so an omitted hand-off cannot silently default to a different interpretation. In generated train_lgbm, use this list as categorical_feature for both training and validation Dataset construction at templates.py:705-725. Encoder selection still uses alias categorical_features. Keep X in config.feature_names order. Predict at :1760-1767 continues passing the transformed NumPy array positionally; do not ask the carried Booster to match aliases by textual name. The OOF array path at :1162-1172 has no original column-name lookup; preserve its existing behavior rather than introducing a separate category-policy change here.

Keep carried model.txt and calibrator_model.txt unchanged. LightGBM already serializes textual feature names, sometimes sanitizing spaces; these are not a reversible label codec. Its pandas_categorical payload contains category values and must not be renamed.

Executed evidence: model_to_string for an integer-named feature contained exactly 'feature_names=7 x'. An additional discriminative 180-row, three-round probe tested labels 'c', 7, 0 and 1 at feature position 0. Original label 1 produced categorical_column=[1], making feature 1 categorical; naive alias retraining instead selected feature 0 and changed predictions by 0.001259999662121647. Label 7 recorded [7] and trained numeric rather than categorical splits on feature 0. Reading the recorded positions after real in-memory Model.export/load and passing [1]/[7] to generated Dataset construction restored maximum prediction difference 0 in both cases. Thus the broad matrix's successful alias prototype is useful evidence but is not sufficient acceptance evidence for native hand-off.

findings.title: Normalize typed frames before every generated name lookup and make file headers explicit
findings.detail:
Embed a shared prepare_input(df, required=()) adapter in both scripts. For an alias-policy project, inspect the entire ordered columns collection, reject MultiIndex, call column_alias on every label, detect duplicate aliases before selection, then assign aliases to a shallow frame copy. Preserve values, dtypes, category metadata, row order and index. Validate extra columns too; after validation, retain the existing behavior of ignoring extra prediction columns. Missing required aliases raise missing_column_alias with the missing aliases and actual offending/input names. Do not guess numeric equivalence, decode bytes names, repair suffixes or reverse 'Unnamed' headers.

Apply this before generated train at templates.py:1463 reads target/features/roles. Independently make directly callable apply_declared_categories (:548), cast_categoricals (:287), fit_pipeline (:340) and train transform (:510) normalize their input before name lookups; repeated normalization of string aliases is idempotent. Helpers retain their existing missing-column behavior, while fit_pipeline requires feature_names. training_order (:577), inner-group selection (:1480) and _resolve_folds (:1087) consume the normalized frame. Train requires features, target and role columns used by its selected time/group/blocked split and inner-validation method; exclusions and absent explicit categorical references are not required input columns. Predict transform (:1686) normalizes before missing/extra checks, category encoding and ordered selection. predict() obtains that path through transform().

Replace direct readers at train :1505, predict :1800 and equivalence :1927 with read_input(path). CSV uses a fixed UTF-8-sig, comma-separated contract: read the raw first logical record with csv.reader(strict=True), validate nonempty UTF-8 names and uniqueness before pandas can mangle them, then read with the corresponding pandas CSV defaults and compare parsed headers with the raw record. Reject blank/invalid headers or raw-to-parsed changes as invalid_column_header; duplicate raw names use column_name_collision. Parquet first inspects Arrow schema names for duplicates, then retains pd.read_parquet so value/dtype semantics stay unchanged. Validate that logical DataFrame columns are strings, flat and unique, and agree with physical data-field names after excluding pandas-declared physical index fields. Required headers must equal project aliases exactly. Do not stringify parquet-returned numeric/None labels or decode a bytes-derived header to an expected alias. Wrap header/parser failures as ValueError-compatible errors with reason and raw/parsed/offending names.

The generated input error reasons are closed: unsupported_column_name, column_name_collision, invalid_column_header, missing_column_alias and column_name_environment_mismatch. Marker/schema errors use the separate reasons listed in the compatibility finding. The exception class exposes reason and context; its message includes the reason and offending names.

test_equivalence.check_equivalence at :1877 continues calling the actual predictor; its CLI uses predict.read_input. In tests/test_codegen/_retrain_harness.py:155, prepare project input with the generated adapter before CSV/parquet writing. Keep the library reference prediction on the original typed frame. Reference-output columns pred/proba are output schema, not training column names.

Executed evidence: all three environments converted CSV integer/float/bool headers to strings; None became 'Unnamed: 0'; duplicate '7,7' became ['7','7.1']; '7,7.1,7' became ['7','7.1','7.2']. Parquet mixed-column round trips stringified numeric names, changed numpy.bytes_(b'c') to 'c', and returned None as None on pandas 2 but NaN on pandas 3. The boundary prototype rejected raw duplicates and blank headers, accepted canonical aliases, rejected missing 'None', and accepted a legitimate literal 'Unnamed: 0' when expected. An already parsed/resaved '7,7.1' is indistinguishable from legitimate names; no validator can detect that lost history. Raw-file validation prevents observable mangling, and producers must canonicalize before writing. The alias prototype passed canonical parquet prediction and the actual generated equivalence checker for all 29 fitted pandas 3 cases.

findings.title: Use an explicit project marker and preserve the unmarked legacy interpretation
findings.detail:
Write column_name_policy='str_alias_v1' in config.json and pipeline_state.json for every new project. The only supported marked value is that exact string; absence means legacy. Null, integers and unknown strings are not absence. Write identical column_name_format objects in both files. Alias-policy readers require well-formed string name lists, unique feature aliases, name-keyed dictionaries whose references belong to the feature schema, identity/stand-in lists that reference categorical features, and agreement between config/state feature order, policy and format. Validate these before _identity_fields or category-value decoding.

The closed marker/schema error reasons are unsupported_column_name_policy, column_name_policy_mismatch and invalid_column_name_state. Context identifies the file/field and expected/actual marker, format or names. If both markers are absent, new scripts use the current unnormalized lookup and legacy state-writing behavior; they must not infer alias policy from JSON string keys or silently repair integer lists. If exactly one marker is absent, prediction refuses the mixed project. Generated train validates its config and writes the same marked or unmarked policy; it does not upgrade an unmarked project by default.

Already-exported scripts do not acquire this mechanism automatically. Regenerate the whole standalone project from the original fitted Model or an unchanged saved Model; copying only new JSON into old scripts is unsupported. Model.export, Model.load, lizyml.persistence.export, runtime fit/predict identity and persistence format versions remain unchanged. Retain category_identity_version independently: column-name policy does not upgrade category identity.

An ordinary all-string project keeps the same column-name values, order, category-value payloads and carried model text, but the new project cannot be byte-for-byte identical: both JSON files gain explicit policy/format metadata and the generated scripts gain policy dispatch and raw-header validation. The positional hand-off and stand-in-plan fields also make project metadata explicit. These format changes must be stated in H-0141 instead of claiming byte preservation. Empty/NUL/non-UTF-8 string names receive the named export refusal defined above. Test byte preservation for carried model files and semantic preservation of all existing ordinary string fields, with the new project fields/source changes enumerated.

Executed evidence: current readers at templates.py:274 and :1559 have no column-name policy dispatch. identity_template.py:55-75 validates membership directly against JSON category keys, reproducing the integer-list/string-key failure in every lane. The actual exported integer-label model text already uses textual '7', so changing its native format is unnecessary.

findings.title: Record firing rates with eligible-project and raw-matrix denominators distinguished
findings.detail:
The recreated critique matrix used the described 25 label families × numeric/object-categorical/declared-category columns, 120 rows, two folds and three boosting rounds. On this head under pandas 3.0.1 it reproduced 29/75 fits, 29/29 prediction-preserving persistence round trips, 12/29 current exports, 10/29 working generated predictors, 12/29 generated retrains and 6/29 ordinary CSV predictors. The two exported integer categorical cases fail identity validation before numeric conversion. Seventeen fitted NumPy-label cases fail current export with raw JSON TypeError. None fails all three fit cases; tuple fails all three. The name-copy prototype exported, predicted and retrained all 29 fitted cases, with maximum prediction difference 0 on that matrix. Canonical CSV/parquet and the actual equivalence checker also passed all 29; the separate discriminative native hand-off finding limits what those totals prove.

Use these activation rates: 23/29 of eligible fitted pandas 3 matrix projects (23 alias projections, 0 proposed name refusals); equivalently 23/75 of original matrix inputs actually reach export and activate. A schema-only classifier over all 75 inputs gives 69/75 activation candidates: 66 non-string aliasable schemas plus 3 unsupported tuple schemas. Those 46 non-fitting inputs are not exported projects and must not be presented as measured exporter refusals. Both older lanes were rerun over the full 75 cases, rather than only the critique's 33-case subset: each had 30 fits/persistence round trips, 13 exports, 11 current generated predictors, 6 ordinary CSV predictors and 30 successful alias-prototype paths. Their eligible activation is 24/30, because numeric None additionally fits.

The bounded suite census gives 0/664 of fitted export_code calls activating, across 665 total attempts including one unfitted call. Measurement: AST enumeration found 80 actual .export_code(...) call sites in 32 files; in-memory pytest execution reached 624 calls at 78 sites, replay of the existing load-census helper's four configurations × five lifecycles × before/after added 40 calls at its site, and the pandas 2 temporal test added one call at the final site. Thus 80/80 inventoried sites were exercised; all 664 fitted schemas were string-only with no proposed name collision/refusal. This is a measured instrumented population, not an unmodified full-suite invocation count. Models were capped at three boosting rounds for the census. Its primary run reported 1,862 passed, 72 failed and 17 skipped; filesystem/subprocess limitations and the tiny-model cap caused failures, so these are not repository regression results.

Each environment printed lizyml.__file__ resolving to this workspace. The missing generated _version module was supplied in memory. No writable temporary directory was available in any lane. JSON/joblib serialization and checksum verification ran against an in-memory filesystem, native model writes used model_to_string, CSV used StringIO and parquet used BytesIO. Real directory/subprocess integration and an unmodified full-suite census could not run under those constraints. No repository edits were made. The activation definition excludes universal marker/template byte changes and measures only non-string alias projection or a name refusal.

findings.title: Give H-0141 closed acceptance criteria and a bounded review stop criterion
findings.detail:
Write H-0141 for v0.21.0 in the H-0139 shape, with numbered 受け入れ基準 and an explicit レビューの停止基準. The acceptance contract should be:

1. Alias rule/DC3: exercise every admitted exact type listed in the alias finding against the library and both generated copies in all three lanes. Fixtures cover both string types; integer widths/signs; 7 versus 7.0; ±0; NaN; ±infinity; small/large exponents; both booleans; bytes with quotes and non-ASCII bytes; complex values; longdouble precision; datetime/timedelta units and NaT; numeric None on pandas 2; and the measured float16/float32 formatting counterexamples. Pin generated function ASTs and exact lane-local aliases. Cross-lane canonical string headers succeed; typed NumPy names under a different recorded format fail with column_name_environment_mismatch. Changed ambient legacy printing must not change a project's aliases.

2. Refusals/collisions: drive every closed name-refusal kind, using tuple, MultiIndex, Decimal, date/datetime, void, arbitrary subclasses, empty/NUL/surrogate text, a conversion failure and an unknown state reference as applicable. Exercise alias collisions for each admitted non-string family against its string alias, duplicate strings, NaN/NaT aliases, and feature/target/time/group/exclude/explicit-categorical/blocked-role/inner-group conflicts. Exercise both Model.export_code and direct generate_code. Assert exact code, surface, reason, kind and offending descriptors, and spy on mkdir/open/write_text/save_model_text to prove zero writes for each refusal, including an existing output directory.

3. Writer inventory: assert every name-bearing field enumerated in these findings contains the expected aliases, in order, after original export and generated retraining. Include categories, modes, declared categories with unused values, identity columns and a genuine nonempty stand-in plan. Assert category-value codec payloads and the original fitted name-bearing containers are unchanged. Repeat from Model.load, including the existing stringified declared-category metadata case. Preserve runtime/persistence predictions without a format-version change.

4. Native hand-off: use discriminative categorical data for original labels 'c', 7, 0 and 1, with the categorical column at position 0. Assert the actual Dataset categorical positions, transformed feature order, native split interpretation and generated retraining predictions. Test original and loaded models. Reject malformed positional metadata explicitly; do not substitute alias-derived positions. Confirm integer 7 is textual '7' in carried model text, and that model/calibrator text bytes are unchanged by project projection.

5. Input boundaries: test typed frames, canonical CSV and canonical parquet through train, predict, retrain-then-predict and the actual equivalence harness. Exercise directly callable cast/declared/fit/transform helpers. Cover duplicate aliases in extra columns, duplicate raw CSV headers, blank None headers, literal 'Unnamed: 0', legitimate suffix names such as '7.1', raw-to-parsed changes, parquet non-string/duplicate/MultiIndex logical names, bytes-header mismatch, missing aliases and reordered features. Assert the five closed input-error reasons and offending names. Preserve category values/dtypes in the in-memory adapter; do not claim recovery of already-lost parser history.

6. Compatibility: fixtures cover both markers absent, valid marked pairs, each one-sided absence, unknown/null/non-string markers, differing formats and malformed alias schemas. Assert the three closed marker/schema reasons. New scripts retain unmarked lookup semantics and unmarked retraining; old standalone projects require full regeneration. Enumerate changed all-string project metadata/source bytes and preserve carried model bytes and existing string-schema semantics.

7. Measurements/documentation: retain per-case matrix results with stable unique IDs, lane versions, original outcomes and designed outcomes; publish the eligible/raw denominators above separately. Add a full-suite export_code census when writable integration is available, reporting normalization, name refusal and their union without counting category-value failures as name failures. Update CHANGELOG, docs/migration.md, codegen documentation and docs/proposal_dispositions.toml for v0.21.0, including the NumPy typed-input environment rule and canonical file-header production.

レビューの停止基準: stop when these closed fixtures, three-lane copy checks, writer inventory, native hand-off checks, compatibility cases and census pass, with environmental integration gaps explicitly recorded. Reopen only for a demonstrated defect in alias computation, collision/refusal diagnostics or ordering, a missed name-bearing site, input-header validation, legacy policy dispatch, state immutability or native positional hand-off. Do not reopen option (e), expand fit/configured-role admission, change runtime persistence/category-value identity, address #391 or alter the tuning fingerprint.

Executed evidence: HISTORY.md:16599-16615 supplies the requested acceptance/stop structure. The executed matrix, boundary prototypes, all 80 call-site census and discriminative LightGBM probe provide concrete fixtures and expected outcomes for this contract; the proposed implementation and its future acceptance suite have not been represented as already completed.
